summary: Five independent attempts to fix the Part-2 ShareRobot direction/motion problem. Duplicated history, noisy depth, and a companion-point depth-resampling bug are all ruled out as the explanation. The clearest pattern: single-frame history (H1-F32) always guesses a confident-but-wrong direction; three-frame history (H3) with a physically COHERENT 3D input (whether honestly-estimated or real measured ground truth) consistently collapses to zero predicted motion instead.

attempt_1_H1F32_single_real_frame_bridge.source: bridge (fixed lab tripod camera over a WidowX arm)

attempt_2_H3_real_frames_noisy_depth.result: zero motion predicted (model likely distrusted an implausible 3D history)

attempt_3_H3_real_frames_consistent_dept.depth: single t0 depth map reused for all 3 frames (physically consistent FOR THE ANCHOR ONLY)
attempt_3_H3_real_frames_consistent_dept.note: predicted direction is close to OPPOSITE the real history direction it was just given
attempt_3_H3_real_frames_consistent_dept.BUG_found_later: the 7 non-anchor query points in this input had a SEPARATE bug: each was re-sampling the depth map at its own shifted 2D location instead of sharing the anchor's depth, giving incoherent per-point displacements (0.05m to 0.77m for points meant to rigidly track one ~3cm gripper -- std 0.33m in depth alone). The anchor's own position (what this cosine is computed from) was not directly affected, but the model was given a physically-incoherent 7-point companion cloud alongside it. See attempt_3b for the same experiment with this bug fixed -- the result changes.

attempt_3b_H3_real_frames_consistent_dep.depth: single t0 depth map; ALL 8 points (anchor + 7 companions) now share one depth value per frame instead of each re-sampling the map -- fixes the attempt_3 bug, otherwise identical setup
attempt_3b_H3_real_frames_consistent_dep.result: ZERO motion predicted (frame-to-frame-IDENTICAL repeating output text -- same degenerate pattern as attempt_4)
attempt_3b_H3_real_frames_consistent_dep.note: With the companion-point bug fixed (physically coherent 8-point cloud, still estimated/assumed depth and intrinsics), the model does NOT repeat attempt_3's confident-wrong-direction answer -- it collapses to zero motion instead, matching attempt_4's real-ground-truth result. This suggests attempt_3's nonzero wrong-direction answer was specifically a response to the incoherent companion points, not a representative 'the model tried and got it wrong' result.

attempt_4_H3_calibrated_REAL_ground_trut.depth: NOT estimated: the exact source BridgeData V2 episode was identified (ShareRobot is a curated subset of several Open-X-Embodiment datasets, 'bridge' among them; matched via instruction-text search in bridge_orig_lerobot's meta/tasks.jsonl, confirmed with a pixel-identical frame-0 match: bridge_orig_lerobot episode_index 45932, task_index 17429). points_3d_history uses the REAL measured 6-DOF WidowX end-effector pose for the anchor point, transformed into camera frame via our own solvePnP-estimated extrinsics (fit on the 8 pre-grasp frames only, where our 2D gripper tracker and the robot's end-effector are the same physical point; mean reprojection error 12.0px on a 640x480 image, i.e. ~2%).
attempt_4_H3_calibrated_REAL_ground_trut.result: ZERO motion predicted (the model's output text is a flat, frame-to-frame-IDENTICAL relative-offset pattern; the anchor's predicted path start == end)
attempt_4_H3_calibrated_REAL_ground_trut.note: The strongest version of the experiment: real, non-duplicated, non-estimated history AND a real (not self-reconstructed) ground-truth future to compare against. The model still fails -- zero predicted motion, same degenerate repeating-text pattern as attempt_3b -- on an input whose real displacement is not small (0.13m history, 0.10m future).

attempt_5_H1F32_single_real_frame_dobbe_.source: dobbe (handheld stick-mounted phone camera, real home -- visually closer to MolmoMotion's strong EgoDex domain than bridge's fixed lab tripod)
attempt_5_H1F32_single_real_frame_dobbe_.hypothesis_tested: does camera framing/domain (not 'robot manipulation' per se) explain the Part-2 failures, given MolmoMotion predicts EgoDex (handheld/egocentric) accurately (1-2cm mean L2 vs authors) but bridge (fixed tripod) poorly
attempt_5_H1F32_single_real_frame_dobbe_.episode: 55_dobbe#episode_3368, action: approach the cabinet door, largest-displacement (250.6px) trajectory-split entry out of 759 dobbe episodes
attempt_5_H1F32_single_real_frame_dobbe_.result: nonzero but very low-confidence/noisy-looking motion predicted (path 0.085m vs GT displacement ~0.28m)
attempt_5_H1F32_single_real_frame_dobbe_.note: Wrong direction, but less extremely wrong than attempt_1's bridge result (-0.62), AND much lower magnitude/confidence -- looks closer to noise than a confident wrong guess. INCONCLUSIVE for the camera-framing hypothesis: H1's structural inability to know direction from 1 frame likely dominates any domain effect. Would need a real multi-frame (H3) dobbe history for a fair test; not pursued further (no planning-split real-video source found/attempted for dobbe).

attempt_6_H3_SECOND_episode_sample_size_.real_or_duplicated: real (planning split, frames 10/16/22 of a DIFFERENT episode -- not episode_4263)
attempt_6_H3_SECOND_episode_sample_size_.why: User's fair challenge: attempts 1-5 all used variations of the SAME single scene (episode_4263, 'move the pan...'). A single scene is too small a sample to conclude the model 'never' works on ShareRobot -- this attempt tests a second, independently-found episode with the same (bug-fixed) methodology, to check if the zero-motion failure is scene-specific or systematic.
attempt_6_H3_SECOND_episode_sample_size_.episode: bridge#episode_4801 ('lift the pot and move it towards the blue cloth'), found via a full tar listing of the planning-split archive (part.aa) cross-referenced against future_prediction_task.json for a clear translation action; frames streamed directly from HuggingFace (a separate network/tooling obstacle was hit and resolved along the way -- see README for the path-prefix bug that was the real cause, not a network issue)
attempt_6_H3_SECOND_episode_sample_size_.depth: estimated (Depth-Anything-V2), FIXED backproject_shared_z method used from the start (no companion-point bug possible here)
attempt_6_H3_SECOND_episode_sample_size_.result: Predicted anchor path is FROZEN at the same 3D point for 28 of 30 predicted frames (a tiny 2-frame blip at frames 5-6, then back to the exact starting value) -- net displacement exactly zero, same degenerate behavior as attempts 3b and 4
attempt_6_H3_SECOND_episode_sample_size_.note: A SECOND, independent scene gives the same qualitative failure (near-total prediction freeze) as the two cleanest attempts on the first scene (3b, 4). This directly answers the small-sample-size concern: the zero-motion collapse is not specific to the pan-episode, it reproduces on a visually and task-wise different episode (pot pick-and-place vs pan push). Also notable: even the REAL motion in this episode reverses direction between history and future (cosine -0.76, since the robot picks up, carries, then sets down) -- a genuinely harder episode to extrapolate than episode_4263's more linear motion, though the model's total prediction freeze doesn't engage with that complexity either way.

attempt_7_H3_SAMPLED_DECODING_not_greedy.why: predict_trajectory() always calls generate() with beam_size=1 and no sampler -- pure GREEDY decoding, a well-known cause of repetitive/degenerate generation when a model is uncertain. molmo_motion/nn/beam_search.py fully supports a `sampler` (MultinomialSampler: temperature-based stochastic decoding) and `constraints` (e.g. RepeatedNGramBlockingConstraint) -- both legitimate, architecturally-provided generation options already built into the released code. NOT a training/finetuning change, NOT a weight change, NOT feeding future frames as input -- purely a decoding-strategy choice, same category as choosing greedy vs. beam-search vs. nucleus sampling for any LLM.
attempt_7_H3_SAMPLED_DECODING_not_greedy.method: re-implemented predict_trajectory()'s logic directly (scripts_local/part2f_sampling_test.py) to pass sampler=MultinomialSampler(temperature=0.8) through to generate(), on the SAME bug-fixed inputs as attempts 3b and 6 (no new data engineering)

episode_4263_pan_temp0.8_seed42.result: NOT frozen -- genuinely varying frame-to-frame text, nonzero net displacement
episode_4263_pan_temp0.8_seed42.note: Weakly positive vs. real future (first-ever positive result on this episode across 7 attempts), though direction vs. its own input history is still poor.

episode_4801_pot_temp0.8_seed42.result: NOT frozen -- genuinely varying frame-to-frame text, nonzero net displacement
episode_4801_pot_temp0.8_seed42.note: Strong positive match -- the best directional result across every attempt in this entire investigation, on either episode.

attempt_7_H3_SAMPLED_DECODING_not_greedy.overall_note: Switching from greedy to temperature-sampled decoding (T=0.8) breaks the degenerate frozen-prediction failure mode on BOTH independent episodes (attempts 3b/6 were frozen at T=0/greedy; both are non-frozen with real, often correctly-directed motion at T=0.8). This is the first manipulation in the entire investigation that improves direction accuracy rather than just changing the failure mode. Caveat: n=1 seed per episode so far -- same lesson as the Part-3 DaS seed-variance finding applies here: a single sample can be an outlier, not yet confirmed with a proper multi-seed sweep. The magnitude of the episode_4801 result (cosine 0.76) is strong enough to be a genuinely promising lead, not just noise, but should be read with that caveat until more seeds are run.

conclusion: Across 6 independently-constructed real (non-duplicated) GREEDY-decoding attempts spanning 2 different ShareRobot/bridge episodes, MolmoMotion never produced a correct, confident future-motion prediction -- greedy decoding (the library's default) consistently either guesses wrong (H1, 1-frame history) or freezes into a degenerate zero-motion repeat (H3, physically coherent 3-frame history). Attempt 7 identifies and fixes the likely root cause of the freezing: greedy decoding itself, a well-documented failure mode for uncertain/out-of-distribution generation. Switching to temperature-sampled decoding (T=0.8, MultinomialSampler, already built into the released library -- not a weight/training change) breaks the freeze on BOTH independently-tested episodes and gives a weakly-to-strongly positive direction match (cosine 0.13 on the pan episode, 0.76 on the pot episode) instead of zero or negative. This reframes the Part-2 story: greedy decoding was likely masking the model's actual (better, though still imperfect and seed-dependent) capability on this domain, not the ShareRobot domain itself being wholly unworkable. Honest caveats: (1) only one seed tested per episode so far -- a proper multi-seed sweep (as was needed to correctly characterize Part 3's DaS variance) is the natural next step before calling this a reliable fix; (2) direction-vs-own-history cosines remain poor in both cases, so the model isn't cleanly extrapolating motion, just producing something less wrong than a frozen/flat answer; (3) this is still zero-shot, consistent with MolmoMotion's own paper (arXiv:2606.18558), which demonstrates robot-domain transfer only via finetuning on DROID, never zero-shot, and never mentions Bridge/WidowX/ShareRobot. The practical conclusion: a legitimate, non-training decoding-strategy change meaningfully improves ShareRobot transfer, but a confident 'it works' claim needs more seeds before it can be made.
